subject: Renewal: Priority pathway — support tier conversion & SLA addendum
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@aurorahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — priority pathway & support uplift

Hi Jonas and Camila,

Thanks for the renewal notice. Aurora Health is preparing our contract renewals for the product analytics and triage pipeline, and we want to discuss converting to a priority support pathway at renewal rather than the current standard plan. Two asks from our side: 

- Formal Premium SLA with defined latency SLOs (we're aiming for p50/p95 targets and credits for sustained misses).
- Capacity uplift: our traffic is expected to grow ~2.3x over the next 12 months. Current committed throughput is 5k qps; we're targeting 12k qps reserved with burst to 18k during peak windows.

Can you outline options (price deltas, commitment lengths, and whether a staged migration or reserved Dedicated pool makes sense)? We need a redline-ready SLA addendum and a high-level capacity plan for our procurement review by 2028-05-20.

Attaching current SOW for reference.

Attachments: [Attachment: Current_SOW.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Sr. Procurement Manager
Aurora Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood-inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood-inference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — priority pathway & support uplift

Maya — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. Appreciate the timeline. High level options so we can align internally and get you a redline-ready addendum: 

1) Premium SLA (annual) — Best for predictable latency and priority ops:
   - Commitment: 12 months (option to extend)
   - Reserved throughput: 12k qps baseline + burst capacity to 18k qps
   - Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 220ms (measured on provisioned endpoints)
   - 15% uplift on your current invoice with a 10% credit buffer for migration windows

2) Priority Lite (12-mo) — Lower-cost path, ops escalation only during business hours:
   - Reserved throughput: 10k qps + burst 14k qps
   - Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 360ms
   - 8% uplift, no migration credit

3) Dedicated Reserved + Ops Add-on — For high-throughput, regulated workflows:
   - Dedicated GPU pool with autoscale policy tuned to your traffic profile
   - SLA targets similar to Premium but with added isolation and encryption controls
   - Pricing: customized; typically 20–30% uplift depending on burst sizing

Recommended next steps:
- Camila: can you draft a capacity ramp and proposed autoscale policy (minutes for scale-up, burst window, warm pool)?
- Priyom: can you prepare a clean SLA addendum draft with the Premium wording and credit language?
- Maya/Procurement: which of the three routes aligns with Aurora's procurement appetite (term length vs. unit economics)?

I attached a CSV with quick-line pricing so procurement can run numbers. Happy to set up a 30-min call early next week to walk through.

Attachments: [Attachment: renewal_options.csv (CSV)]

—
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Maya Singh <maya@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood-inference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 04 May 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — capacity ramp and operational plan

Hi team — looping in some technical constraints and a suggested runbook for the capacity increase. High-level notes: 

- Staged reserved capacity: move to a 12k baseline over three months (4k increments per month) with burst pool available during peak windows. This reduces warm-up costs and lets us tune KV/cache priming.
- Autoscaling policy: 2-minute aggressive scale-up (to catch short spikes), 15–30 minute scale-down to avoid thrash.
- KV cache priming: for your high reuse models, we recommend prefix caching for the most frequent flows (we can share a list of top 50 prefixes to pre-warm).
- Monitoring: we can add a per-route dashboard and set automated regression alerts (if p95 increases > 30% for two consecutive days).

Proposed SLA addendum language (summary):
- Scope: Only applies to Redwood-managed production inference endpoints listed in SOW.
- SLOs: p50 and p95 latency targets measured at the API edge; credits issued for sustained p95 misses beyond a 2-hour window; force majeure carve-outs as standard.
- Operational support: 24/7 incident routing for Premium; response windows defined per severity (P1: 1 hour, P2: 4 hours).

I'll attach a simple capacity plan sheet that maps committed throughput to expected GPU pools and estimated cost buckets. Priyom — if you can translate the summary above into contract language, we should be ready to provide a redline.

Attachments: [Attachment: capacity_plan.xlsx (XLSX)]

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Maya Singh <maya@aurorahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@aurorahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 09 May 2028 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Priority pathway — support tier conversion & SLA addendum

Thanks all — this is helpful and in line with what procurement expects. Aurora prefers the Premium SLA (option 1) with a 12-month term and the staged ramp you outlined. A few follow-ups before we finalize: 

1) Can Redwood include a one-time migration credit to cover parallel run costs? We'd like an explicit credit equal to one invoice period (or equivalent) during ramp month 1.
2) Please send the redline-ready SLA addendum and the renewal quote (line items by month for committed throughput).
3) We'll need a short annex that confirms the autoscale windows and the warm pool sizing so our cloud team can plan network and egress.

If you can get the addendum and quote over by COB Friday (2028-05-12) we'll route internally for signature. Otherwise let's book a 30-minute call Friday morning to close outstanding items.

Requested attachments for your submission: SLA_Addendum_draft.docx (redline-ready), final renewal_options.csv with line-item pricing, and the capacity_plan.xlsx with warm-pool sizing.

Best,
Maya Singh
Sr. Procurement Manager
Aurora Health
